Klean by Geerho Hardware Guide

How to connect coin-operated washers and dryers to Klean so customers can pay by scanning a QR code. Your machines keep accepting coins as before.

Safety first. The Klean controller connects only to the machine's low-voltage coin signal. Anything that touches the 220 V supply (fitting current sensors at the breaker panel) must be done by a licensed electrician. Unplug the machine before opening it, and check your machine's warranty first.

How it works

  1. A customer scans the machine's QR code in the Klean app and pays.
  2. Klean tells the controller to add a credit. The controller clicks a relay wired across the coin acceptor's signal wire, once per coin, so the machine sees coins. The machine's light in Klean turns white (paid, press Start).
  3. The customer presses Start on the machine, or taps Start wash / Start dry in Klean after confirming the laundry is in and the door is closed. Klean never starts a machine by itself. A current sensor on the machine's power line notices the motor running and the controller reports started (light blue).
  4. When the machine has been stopped for 3 minutes, the controller reports completed (light green) and the customer gets a "laundry is done" notification.

Start from the app. When the customer taps Start in Klean, the controller gets a START command. It presses the machine's Start button through an optional second relay wired across that button (set START_PINS in the firmware), or, for machines that start as soon as coins go in, it holds the coins until START (tick "These machines start as soon as coins go in" before downloading the controller file). Without either, START is ignored and the customer presses Start on the machine. Controller files downloaded before October 18, 2026 need downloading again.

One controller box runs up to 4 machines. A laundromat with 6 washers and 6 dryers needs 3 boxes.

How to connect one machine

Coin acceptor ──┬── COIN signal ──► machine control board
                │
Relay  NO ──────┘        relay contact in parallel with the coin acceptor's output
Relay  COM ───────────── GND of the coin circuit
Relay  IN  ◄──────────── ESP32 pin (one per machine)

Current switch, clamped on the machine's LIVE wire at its breaker (electrician)
  output contact ──────── ESP32 input pin and GND
  1. Find the coin acceptor's signal wire (often white, labelled COIN) and its ground. Set the acceptor to pulse output (most are by default).
  2. Count how many coins one cycle costs on the machine (e.g. six ₱10 coins). That's the pulses number you enter when you download the controller file.
  3. Connect the relay's NO and COM across COIN and GND, in parallel with the acceptor. The relay is a dry contact, so the controller never shares power with the machine.
  4. Have an electrician clamp a current switch around each machine's live wire (one wire only, not the whole cable) and set it to close when the motor runs. Wire its contact to the controller's input for that machine.
  5. Mount the box away from water, steam and dryer heat.

Default pins (LILYGO T-Relay): relays on 21, 19, 18, 5; current switch inputs on 32, 33, 25, 26. Change them at the top of the firmware for other boards.

Software

  1. On a computer, open Klean HQ, choose the location, and set the machines with controllers to Real.
  2. Hardware → Download controller file. Enter the coins per cycle. The file (klean_config.h) holds each machine's secret key: keep it private, and delete it after flashing. Downloading again issues new keys, so every box at that location must be flashed again.
  3. Install the Arduino IDE 2, add the esp32 boards package (Espressif) and the ArduinoJson library.
  4. Open klean-hub.ino, put klean_config.h next to it, enter your Wi-Fi name and password in the file, set KLEAN_BOX_NUMBER (1 for the first box, 2 for the second…), connect the board by USB, and click Upload.
  5. Power the box. Within a minute the machines turn green in Klean HQ and the app.

NFC tap stickers (optional)

Next to each machine's QR sticker you can add an NFC sticker, so customers just tap their phone on it.

  • Buy: NTAG213 (or NTAG215/216) NFC stickers, round 25–30 mm, about ₱15–30 each. On a metal machine use anti-metal (on-metal) NFC stickers, or the tag won't read through the steel.
  • Write: in the Klean app, Business → Setup → Branches → the branch → the machine's menu → Write NFC sticker (Android: NFC) → Write and lock. Hold the blank sticker against the phone; it gets the same link as the machine's QR and is locked, so nobody can rewrite it to point somewhere else (locking is permanent; use Write without locking (test) for trying things out).
  • Place: right beside the QR, at a comfortable height. Optional: a small "Tap or scan to pay" label.
  • Customers: iPhone (XS or newer) and most Android phones read it by just touching the sticker with the phone unlocked; Klean opens on that machine. iPhone users can also tap Tap NFC sticker on the Scan screen.

Klean Scale (optional)

A laundry scale that sends each settled weight to Klean. Customers tap Use the Klean Scale in Start laundry instead of typing the kilos.

  • Buy: a platform (bench) scale of 30–60 kg with a standard 4-wire load cell, certified for trade (in the Philippines it must be tested and sealed by your city or municipal treasurer's weights and measures office, renewed every 6 months), an HX711 load-cell amplifier board (₱80–150), an ESP32 DevKit V1 (₱250–450) and a 5 V USB supply. Total for the electronics: about ₱500–800.
  • Connect: load cell red/black/white/green → HX711 E+/E−/A−/A+ (check your cell's colour code). HX711 VCC → ESP32 3V3, GND → GND, DT → GPIO 16, SCK → GPIO 4. Keep it dry; mount the board under the platform.
  • Set up: in the Klean app, Business → Setup → Branches → the branch → + Add a Klean Scale. Copy the Controller ID and Secret (shown once) into firmware/klean-scale/klean-scale.ino with your Wi-Fi details, upload it with the Arduino IDE (library "HX711" by Bogdan Necula), then calibrate: empty the scale, type t in the Serial Monitor; put a known weight on it (a 5 kg bag of rice) and type c 5000; copy the printed factor into the file and upload again.
  • Check: put something on it. Within about 2 seconds of the number settling, the branch's Klean Scale card in the app shows the weight. In Start laundry, Use the Klean Scale fills it in.
  • Rules: one weight is sent per load; nothing more is sent until the scale is emptied. Each weighing can be used once, within 2 minutes. Attendants use it at the counter too (Work → Intake → Use the Klean Scale). Business → Require the scale stops typed weights in Start laundry and at the counter.

Test before opening

Scan each machine's QR in the Klean app and pay. You should hear one relay click per coin and see the light turn white; press Start (on the machine, or Start wash in the app) and it turns blue. Nothing should start before that. If a light is red:

Red reasonCheck
Controller offline (no heartbeat)Wi-Fi name/password, power, signal strength at the machine
Controller did not confirm creditRelay wiring, box number, the machine's controller ID in the file
FaultLook at the machine; clear the error in the app (Work → machine → Clear)

Good to know

  • Coins still work. A coin-paid cycle isn't shown in Klean (the light stays green while the machine runs).
  • Klean only works online. If the internet drops, QR payments stop until it's back; coins keep working.
  • Controllers check Klean's security certificate, so a box with the wrong date or a blocked network won't connect.
